subject: GCP Marketplace promotional credit stacking — channel margin reconciliation
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Allen <ops@distributorx.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify promotional credit stacking on GCP PO - impact to Partner invoice

Hi Naomi,

Quick one: attached is the PO snapshot we received from GCP for the upcoming Acme Health private offer. It looks like two promotional credits applied at listing level (early-adopter and regional rebate) stacked against the line items. DistributorX says those credits were applied post-listing and are reducing the invoice amount they receive, which in turn is putting their margin negative after the agreed reseller pass-through.

Can you confirm how Redwood is seeing the credits on your side and whether there's a standard pass-through mechanism for marketplace credits to avoid squeezing the partner? This is blocking DistributorX from invoicing—procurement needs net payable confirmation before we sign the PO addendum.

Attachment: acme_po_snapshot.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Acme Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Mike Allen <ops@distributorx.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify promotional credit stacking on GCP PO - impact to Partner invoice

Thanks for flagging — looping in Sales Ops (Ben), Deal Ops (Camila) and Finance (Irene) to triage. Full disclosure: marketplace promotional credits can be applied at multiple levels (listing, billing account, regional rebate) and GCP sometimes offers stacking that reduces the list price before the distributor's share calculation. That can create the negative-margin outcome you're seeing.

Camila/Ben/Irene — can you review the attached PO snapshot and the partner's margin workback and confirm where the pass-through mismatch is occurring? If DistributorX cannot pass the credit through in the GCP flow, we'll need a commercial workaround (amortization, one-time reimbursement, or a list-price uplift) before Acme signs.

Mike — if you can send the partner's invoice copy or a quick margin calc that shows the shortfall that will help speed this up.

I'll propose concrete options once we have the workback.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Mike Allen <mike.allen@distributorx.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify promotional credit stacking on GCP PO - impact to Partner invoice

Appreciate the quick loop-in. Attached is our invoice and the margin workback showing a ~ -7% margin after Redwood's agreed reseller pass-through when both the early-adopter promo (USD 40k) and the regional rebate (USD 25k) are applied. In short, GCP applied those credits against the invoice before the distributor fee calculation, so DistributorX received less gross revenue to split.

We do not have an automatic way in our billing flow to reclaim those credits from Acme or GCP post-invoice; our only practical remedies today are: 1) ask Redwood to reimburse the partner for the delta, 2) increase the list price on the marketplace so credits don't push net below reseller share, or 3) amortize the impact across future months and settle once usage ramps.

Attachment: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (xlsx)

Mike
Ops Lead, DistributorX
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Options + quick numbers for Acme / DistributorX

Short note with options and estimated P&L impact (quick calc):

Option A — Redwood one-time reimbursement to DistributorX: covers the delta for the initial invoice. Estimated cost: USD 18,500 (covers the -7% gap per workback). Pros: fixes procurement blocker immediately. Cons: non-recurring cash hit and sets expectation.

Option B — Amortize the credit impact over 6 months (60/40 split Redwood/DistributorX): Redwood impact ~ USD 11,000 over six months, partner keeps invoice cadence and margin recovers gradually. Pros: cash smoothing. Cons: requires partner buy-in and a short amendment to the reseller agreement.

Option C — Update GCP marketplace listing price to absorb expected credits (list-price uplift ~ 3.5%): longer-term fix, requires marketplace team change and re-approval from Acme procurement. Pros: scalable. Cons: slower and may trigger extra procurement review.

Recommended: go Option B as compromise while we implement C as product fix. If Procurement needs a signature today, propose a limited PO addendum where Redwood guarantees the amortized reimbursement schedule.

Irene — can Finance confirm accounting treatment for the amortized reimbursement (expense vs. contra-revenue)?

Ben
Director, Sales Ops
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Mike Allen <mike.allen@distributorx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify promotional credit stacking on GCP PO - impact to Partner invoice

Thanks all — quick update and proposed path forward so procurement can close:

Agreement summary (proposed):
- Redwood will absorb 60% of the initial credit-driven shortfall and DistributorX will absorb 40%. We will amortize the Redwood portion over 6 months and pay DistributorX a one-time settlement equal to the first two months of the amortized amount to remove immediate cash pressure.
- Redwood will open a ticket with our Marketplace team to implement a 3.5% list-price uplift for this SKU family to prevent similar stacking from creating negative-margin outcomes in future POs; changes will be communicated to Acme procurement once the uplift is scheduled (estimated 3-4 weeks).
- DistributorX to provide an invoice and final margin calc by EOD tomorrow; Redwood will issue the settlement by next Wednesday and the six-month amortization schedule will be captured in a PO addendum / DocuSign amendment.

Attachments: gcp_marketplace_credit_matrix.csv (csv) — internal reference of credit stacking rules we used in the calc.
Related: PO addendum draft (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.com/Tx/ABC1234
Drive workback: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1gcp-credit-matrix
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/9843/deal/DEAL-9843

Mike / Procurement Team — please confirm acceptance of the above compromise so we can get the DocuSign addendum signed today. If Procurement insists on a different split, flag the alternative and we'll escalate.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
